newsitem.title: UK: S&N calls for consultation on minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: S&N calls for consultation on minimum wage.

text.p: Britain's largest brewer Scottish & Newcastle Plc called on the newly-elected Labour party on Friday to consult widely on its plans to introduce a minimum wage.
"Labour has committed to consulting widely on the minimum wage and it is essential that such consultation takes place," said S&N, which employs some 28,000 people in its pubs and restaurants.

The company said the minimum wage "cannot sensibly be based only on hourly base rate" but must also take account of other elements like pensions and incentives, food and lodging and employer's investment in staff training.

The company said if Scotland was given powers over taxation it would have an adverse effect on S&N if those rates differed from the rest of the country and would "reduce the likelihood of increased investment by the company in Scotland".

S&N also reiterated the industry's demands for lower excise duties on beer in Britain to come into line with those in mainland Europe. Lower excise duties would generate more pub jobs and benefit the government's public sector borrowing requirement, said the company. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
